subject: BinaryStar-3b elevated 5xxs — availability brief & next steps
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, rachel.kim@redwood.ai, ops@binarystar.ai
Cc: support@binarystar.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Aug 2029 08:12:00 -0000
Subject: BinaryStar-3b elevated 5xxs — availability brief & next steps

Team,

We observed an uptick in 5xx and timeout errors originating from the BinaryStar-3b model serving pool starting ~08:00Z. Errors are concentrated on the rw-binarystar-3b-v2 model variant (tokenization + kv-cache path). Impact: increased request failures and sporadic latency spikes for BinaryStar.ai customers on the us-west region.

What we know so far:
- First anomalous spike detected by anomaly-alert at 07:55Z.
- Errors are 502/504 and stream timeouts; not a control-plane outage.
- Autoscaling is behaving normally; affected requests show repeated KV cache misses and a build-up of in-flight partial states.

Immediate actions (in flight):
- Marcus is running targeted kernel telemetry to confirm whether a new runtime kernel path triggered this.
- Neha is isolating affected GPU pool and preparing a canary redirect to rw-binarystar-3b-v1 (lower latency profile) as temporary mitigation.
- Rachel, please prepare a short external notification for BinaryStar SRE (ops@binarystar.ai) with rollback/fallback guidance.

Grace O'Connor
Sr. Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: binarystar_error_slice_0816.log (excerpt), binarystar_kvcache_trace_0816.txt
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, rachel.kim@redwood.ai, ops@binarystar.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Aug 2029 09:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: BinaryStar-3b elevated 5xxs — availability brief & next steps

Grace / all,

Quick triage update: we confirmed a regression in the kv-cache eviction logic in the rw-binarystar-3b-v2 runtime path. Under a particular request mix (long prefixes + streaming), the eviction routine can race with concurrent kv writes, causing invalidated pointers and partial response errors — manifests as 502s/stream terminations.

Actions taken 09:00–09:30Z:
- Rolled a config to disable the new eviction heuristic on the affected pool; this immediately reduced the 5xx rate by ~65% in the canary group.
- Initiated a controlled fallback: 25% of traffic redirected to rw-binarystar-3b-v1 for BinaryStar.ai route; observing improved success and stable latency.
- Captured additional traces (attached).

Next: full rollback of the heuristic to the stable eviction policy if telemetry remains green after the 30m observation window. Will keep you posted.

Marcus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Sara / BinaryStar ops team,

Thanks — short answers:
1) Marcus' team is observing the canary now (25% traffic). If the 30-minute observation window remains stable (no reproducible 502s/504s), we will promote the rollback and route 100% of BinaryStar.ai traffic to the stable eviction policy. Targeting full promotion by 19:00Z this evening (approx ETA: ~40–60 minutes).
2) Temporary client guidance: increase client-side retry delay to 300–500ms with exponential backoff and cap retries to 2. Avoid aggressive immediate retries (this can amplify in-flight load). If you can, enqueue longer prompt jobs to the non-streaming endpoint (rw-binarystar-3b-v1) for the next 2 hours — that's where we've routed the canary workload.

We'll share a postmortem draft once we complete the rollback and have the final traces. Apologies for the disruption — we understand the downstream impact and are prioritizing closure.

Grace O'Connor
Sr. Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 17 Aug 2029 14:35:00 -0000
Subject: BinaryStar-3b incident closure and postmortem (draft)

BinaryStar ops / Sara,

Closure summary (final):
- Timeline: root cause identified 16 Aug 08:55Z; rollback initiated 16 Aug 09:00Z; full promotion to stable eviction policy completed 16 Aug 19:05Z; error rates returned to baseline by 16 Aug 19:25Z.
- Impact: elevated 502/504 and stream timeouts for ~4 hours; peak failed request rate ~18% for BinaryStar.ai route; degraded user-facing latency for a subset of long-prefix streaming workloads.
- Root cause: a regression in the kv-cache eviction heuristic introduced a race condition under concurrent writes, causing corrupted in-memory pointers and partial responses.
- Mitigation: immediate rollback of heuristic, canary routing to rw-binarystar-3b-v1, client guidance on retry/backoff.
- Remediation: engineering is preparing a fix that replaces the heuristic with a lock-free, reference-counted approach and adds aggressive fuzz tests for concurrent kv operations. Planned deployment: 2029-08-20 after QA.

We've attached the forensic logs and an editable postmortem draft: binarystar_error_slice_0816.log, binarystar_kvcache_trace_0816.txt, binarystar_postmortem-draft.pdf.

Action items for BinaryStar.ai:
- Optional: adopt a 300–500ms retry delay with capped retries for the next 48 hours.
- We will schedule a 30-minute sync on Monday to walk through remediation and QA verification (proposed: Mon 2029-08-19 16:00Z).

Please reply with any questions or if you'd like an earlier sync.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference
